plan: This ascending clock auction with sealed exit bids functions as a second-price auction: I win if my bid is highest, and I pay the second-highest bid, not my own. Therefore, bidding my true value ($25) is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit since I only pay less than my bid when I win, and bidding higher or lower than true value only risks either overpaying or losing profitable opportunities. No history exists to suggest otherwise.

In this ascending clock auction with sealed exit bids, the mechanism is equivalent to a second-price auction: I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. Bidding my true value ($17) is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit since bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth, and bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. I'll bid exactly my value.

This mechanism functions like a second-price auction: my sealed bid sets my exit point, and I win only if I have the highest bid, paying the second-highest bid. Bidding exactly my true value ($39) is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit since I only pay less than my value if I win, and bidding higher or lower than value only reduces expected profit without changing the price I'd pay when winning.
